Byte-Latent Modeling

Install Blog GitHub

Byte-Latent Modeling in Gollek

For the guided docs landing page that groups architecture, terminal workflow, repo locations, and stable-vs-evolving notes in one place, start with Byte-Latent Docs. For the compact terminal grammar lookup page, use Byte-Latent Inspector Reference.

Gollek treats byte-latent language modeling as a separate architecture family, not as an extension of diffusion training.

That means Fast Byte Latent Transformer style work belongs in dedicated language-modeling modules such as gollek-ml-byte-latent, with reuse of shared core/runtime pieces where appropriate.

Why It Is Separate

  • the model operates on byte-native inputs rather than token-only pipelines
  • the architecture introduces byte-latent encoder/decoder concerns
  • the trainer and runner paths should evolve independently from diffusion OPD

Current Code Direction

The first concrete package root is:

  • gollek/ml/gollek-ml-byte-latent

Initial Java contracts include:

  • ByteSequenceBatch
  • ByteSequenceCollator
  • ByteSequenceWindowBatch
  • TextByteSequenceDataset
  • ByteLatentTrainerConfig
  • ByteLatentTrainingPlan
  • ByteLatentTrainerSupport
  • ByteLatentTrainer
  • ByteLatentTrainerSession
  • ByteLatentState
  • ByteLatentModelSpec
  • ByteLatentModel
  • ByteLatentForwardPass
  • ByteLatentGenerationResult
  • ReferenceByteLatentModel
  • ByteLatentEncoder
  • ByteLatentDecoder
  • ReferenceByteLatentMixer
  • ReferenceByteLatentProjection
  • ReferenceByteLatentOutputHead
  • ByteLatentTransformerBlock
  • ByteLatentModelFamily

Paper Citation

  • Julie Kallini, Artidoro Pagnoni, Tomasz Limisiewicz, Gargi Ghosh, Luke Zettlemoyer, Christopher Potts, Xiaochuang Han, and Srinivasan Iyer. Fast Byte Latent Transformer. arXiv:2605.08044v1, 2026.

Current Data Flow Primitive

The next step after raw byte batches is causal language-model packing.

ByteSequenceCollator.causalLanguageModeling(...) converts raw byte sequences into:

  • padded inputIds
  • shifted targetIds
  • attention masks

This gives Gollek a byte-native training batch shape before the heavier trainer and runner modules arrive.

Current Inference Primitive

ByteLatentModel now exposes a minimal executable inference surface:

  • predictNextToken(int[])
  • predictNextTokens(int[], topK)
  • generate(int[], maxNewTokens)

ByteLatentPreviewFormatter.nextTokensPreview(...) provides the shared compact preview encoding used by the current byte-latent inference demos and persisted train-infer report artifacts.

ReferenceByteLatentModel provides the first deterministic implementation of that surface. It now routes batches through a concrete reference encode -> latent-mix -> latent-project -> latent-transform -> decode -> output-head pipeline using ReferenceByteLatentEncoder, ReferenceByteLatentMixer, ReferenceByteLatentProjection, ReferenceByteLatentDecoder, and ReferenceByteLatentOutputHead, so the module is starting to look more like a real byte-latent architecture instead of a purely direct token transform.

Current Dataset Bridge

TextByteSequenceDataset is the first ingestion bridge for byte-latent work. It can load UTF-8 text lines, expose them as byte sequences, and emit ByteSequenceBatch slices that feed directly into ByteSequenceCollator.causalLanguageModeling(...).

Current Trainer Prep Surface

ByteLatentTrainerConfig and ByteLatentTrainerSupport.plan(...) provide the first trainer-facing API for this family.

That lets Gollek build deterministic trainer-ready batches from:

  • raw UTF-8 text lines
  • byte batches
  • packed causal-LM windows

without coupling byte-latent work to the diffusion or generic trainer stacks too early.

Current Executable Trainer Surface

ByteLatentTrainer.builder() now turns that prep surface into an executable session. The current implementation is intentionally lightweight:

  • builds trainer-ready batches from the dataset/config pair
  • iterates epochs and batches deterministically
  • accepts a pluggable batch-loss evaluator
  • exposes byte-latent lifecycle listener hooks
  • writes lightweight summary and manifest artifacts when checkpointDir is set
  • writes byte-latent-history.csv with one row per completed epoch
  • writes byte-latent-report.json with summary, history, and artifact paths
  • can resume epoch/best-loss/global-step state from those artifacts when resumeFromCheckpoint is enabled, including the persisted history timeline
  • exposes compact history: selectors for terminal queries such as history:summary, history:lastLoss, and history:sort=-trainLoss:top=3
  • emits a TrainingSummary with byte-latent metadata

That gives the byte-latent family its first runnable training session contract without pretending the full optimization/runtime stack is already finished.

Terminal Inspection

Gollek now has a small JBang entrypoint for byte-latent checkpoint history:

trainer_byte_latent_history_inspector.java

And an end-to-end checkpoint producer:

trainer_byte_latent_demo.java

And a matching resume walkthrough:

trainer_byte_latent_resume_demo.java

And a tiny inference walkthrough:

trainer_byte_latent_infer_demo.java

And a combined train-then-infer walkthrough:

trainer_byte_latent_train_infer_demo.java

It also writes train-infer-report.json with a stable top-level reportVersion schema marker plus machine-readable training and inference sections, including both nextTokens and persisted nextTokensPreview, plus persisted top-level overview, overviewCi, status, statusSummary, commands, commandsCi, selectors, selectorsCi, inspectfields, inspectfieldsCi, artifactSummary, and artifactSummaryLine.

trainer_byte_latent_train_infer_inspector.java reads that report from a checkpoint directory or direct file path and supports compact selectors such as reportVersion, artifactSummary, artifactSummaryLine, overview, overview:ci, training, inference, nextToken, nextTokens, nextTokensPreview, generatedText, combinedText, commands, commands:ci, selectors, selectors:ci, inspectfields, inspectfields:ci, statusSummary, status, health, and ci.

trainer_byte_latent_train_infer_compare_inspector.java compares two of those reports and supports workflow-style selectors such as overview, runs, status, health, ci, left, right, and delta:* selectors like delta:latestTrainLoss, delta:nextToken, delta:nextTokens, delta:nextTokensPreview, delta:nextTokensCount, and delta:combinedText. Those direct compare outputs now also include reportVersion plus leftReportVersion / rightReportVersion so live compares and exported compare bundles expose the same schema-version signal. It also supports resultStatus / resultStatus:ci as a matching artifact-centric status alias family for reopened standalone compare-result files. It also persists top-level commands / commandsCi, selectors / selectorsCi, and inspectfields / inspectfieldsCi so the exported compare result has the same compact discovery vocabulary as the bundle path. Direct compare mode now also supports compareSummaryLine as a one-line shell-friendly summary to match the exported compare bundle’s comparisonSummary. It also supports bundle=standard to export a small compare bundle with overview.json, runs.json, delta-nextTokens.json, delta-nextTokensPreview.json, delta-nextTokensCount.json, other key delta-*.json files, and manifest.json. The same inspector can reopen those exported bundle directories with bundleSummary, comparisonSummary, bundleFiles, bundleManifest, file:<name>, and loadfile:<section>. It also supports commands and commands:ci for recommended compare-bundle follow-up selectors, plus inspectfields and inspectfields:ci for machine-readable field discovery. It also supports bundleHealth and filesSummary:by=section|format for compact compare-bundle integrity and file-count summaries. Exported compare bundle manifests also persist those recommendations in top-level commands and commandsCi, alongside the legacy inspectCommands and inspectCommandsCi, plus top-level shortcuts in inspectBundleStatus, inspectBundleHealth, inspectBundleOverview, inspectBundleFiles, and inspectBundleLoadfile. They also persist field discovery in top-level inspectfields and inspectfieldsCi, alongside the legacy inspectFields and inspectFieldsCi. They also persist artifactSummary and artifactSummaryLine for a compact bundle-dashboard block and one-line summary. They now also carry a stable top-level reportVersion plus leftReportVersion / rightReportVersion source markers for schema-aware automation. They now also expose selectors and selectors:ci so bundle consumers get a compact direct-query discovery surface without deriving it from the larger manifest fields. They also include a compact comparison block plus top-level leftNextTokensPreview, rightNextTokensPreview, and nextTokensPreviewChanged fields for lightweight automation. They also include a one-line comparisonSummary string for simple CI or shell output. They also expose top-level selector hints in inspectBundleSummarySelector, inspectBundleFilesSummarySelector, inspectBundleNextTokensSelector, inspectBundleNextTokensPreviewSelector, inspectBundleNextTokensCountSelector, inspectBundleMissingFilesSelector, and inspectBundleMissingFilesTopSelector. They also expose a compact status block in status, plus mirrored top-level scalars in healthStatus, missingFileCount, and okFileCount. They also expose statusSummary as a human-readable one-line health/status string. filesSummary also supports sort=-count and top=<n> for trimmed compare-bundle rollups. bundleHealth also supports focus=files|sections|formats|all, sort=..., and top=<n> for trimmed health diagnostics. bundleStatus and bundleHealth:ci provide one-line compare-bundle health checks for CI or quick terminal scans. bundleOverview and bundleOverview:ci provide a more consistent compare-bundle overview path alongside the workflow bundle inspector. loadfile: also supports section=<section>, pick=first|last, and index=<n> so repeated compare bundle sections can be reopened deterministically. bundleFiles also supports filtered listing through files:section=..., files:name=..., files:format=..., sort=..., and top=<n>. bundleHealth:focus=files also supports section=..., name=..., format=..., and status=ok|missing for filtered per-file health diagnostics. Those same filters also apply before grouped bundleHealth:focus=sections|formats rollups.

Both scripts now print status, health, and ci follow-up inspector commands automatically at the end of a run.

And a one-command smoke helper:

run_byte_latent_smoke.sh

And a matching one-command resume smoke helper:

run_byte_latent_resume_smoke.sh

Both smoke helpers now lead with status, health, and ci inspector checks before the more detailed history queries.

The unified workflow launcher now does the same in its final suggested commands, surfacing status, health, and ci before the longer inspector forms, and leading with status and health across checkpoint, manifest, and bundle checks. It now also surfaces commands:summary first on the workflow-manifest side for the compact command rollup. Each fresh/resume run summary also prints runcommands:<run> alongside commands:ci:mode=<run> for the matching single-line manifest-driven CI follow-up. That workflow-manifest block now also includes runcommands, runcommands:ci, runcommands:fresh, and runcommands:resume as the shortest discovery and per-run aliases, and runcommands:all as the concise multi-run alias summary. The launcher also prints inspectfields there as the full machine-readable field-discovery selector, and inspectfields:ci as the compact machine-readable field-discovery summary. The launcher also prints runfields:ci as the compact per-run field-discovery summary, and runfields as the per-run field-discovery selector. Each fresh/resume run summary also prints runfields:ci as the compact per-run field-discovery hint. Each fresh/resume run summary also prints runcommands:ci as the generic compact discovery hint for available per-run aliases. Each fresh/resume run summary also prints runcommands:all as the concise multi-run alias overview path.

And a unified workflow launcher:

run_byte_latent_workflow.sh

In full mode it now finishes with a compact summary covering both the fresh and resumed checkpoint runs, including history row counts and inspector-ready commands.

The launcher also writes a small workflow manifest JSON so CI or follow-up scripts can consume the same fresh/resume run details without parsing terminal text.

That manifest now also records workflowBundleDir and workflowBundleStatus, so downstream tools can discover whether the bundle was materialized and where it lives without reconstructing the path. It also records inspectWorkflowStatus, inspectWorkflowHealth, inspectBundleStatus, and inspectBundleHealth, so automation can reuse the same recommended status and health entrypoints the launcher prints for humans. Each per-run manifest entry now also records inspectWorkflowCommands for the single-line commands:ci:mode=<run> workflow follow-up. Each per-run manifest entry now also records inspectRunCommands for the shortest runcommands:<run> workflow follow-up. Each per-run manifest entry now also records inspectRunAll for the concise multi-run runcommands:all workflow overview path. Each per-run manifest entry now also records inspectRunFields for the compact inspectfields:ci machine-readable field-discovery hint.

In full mode it now also materializes the workflow bundle automatically, so the printed loadfile: examples point at a real bundle directory immediately.

Gollek now also includes a matching workflow-manifest inspector so those JSON artifacts can be queried from the terminal with selectors like runs, workflowBundleDir, run:fresh, historyRows, and delta:historyRows.

When the manifest reports workflowBundleStatus=materialized, that same inspector can also jump straight into the bundle with selectors like bundleManifest, bundleFiles, bundleSummary, and bundleLoadfile:section=runs.

For a compact terminal-friendly bundle check, bundleOverview summarizes the bundle path, status, availability, file count, and health in one small view. It also supports focus=health, focus=files, and focus=all. Plain text output is optimized for terminal scanning, while json remains available for automation. For CI logs, summary=short collapses the text output to a single line. bundleOverview:ci is the shorthand alias for the recommended CI-style overview check. status is the shortest neutral alias when you just want one concise bundle-status line, and bundleStatus remains available as the explicit form. health is the matching shortest direct-health alias when you want the bundle-health view first. commands renders the manifest’s recommended inspector commands as a small table, with optional filters like scope=workflow and mode=fresh. commands:summary and commands:ci collapse that to the most important workflow, bundle, and fresh/resume checkpoint status-health commands. commands:ci:mode=<run> turns that into a single-line per-run compact command rollup for fresh or resume. runcommands lists the available per-run aliases from the manifest. runcommands:all expands to the concise multi-run alias summary. runcommands:summary and runcommands:ci collapse that discovery view into compact manifest-level run-alias summaries. runcommands:<run> is the shortest alias for that per-run manifest rollup. runfields lists the per-run inspectRunFields, inspectRunCommands, and inspectRunAll follow-up aliases together. runfields:summary and runfields:ci collapse that per-run field-discovery view into compact manifest-level summaries. runfields:<run> isolates that per-run field-discovery row for one run mode. inspectfields lists which machine-readable inspector-command fields are present at the manifest and per-run levels. inspectfields:summary and inspectfields:ci collapse that field-discovery view into compact terminal and CI summaries. The same one-line path is also available on bundleHealth, with bundleHealth:ci as a shorthand alias.

The workflow launcher now prints those manifest-inspector commands directly at the end of each run, alongside the checkpoint history inspector commands.

It also prints the workflow-bundle export and loadfile: commands so the deeper bundle navigation path is visible immediately after a run completes.

For shareable artifacts, the workflow inspector also supports bundle=standard, which writes overview, runs, and delta views into a single output directory with its own bundle manifest.

Those exported workflow bundles can then be inspected directly with bundleSummary, bundleHealth, files, files:section=<section>, files:name=<name>, file:<name>, and loadfile:section=<section>, similar to the diffusion report bundle flow.

For ordered bundle listings, files: also supports sort=name, sort=section, and sort=format.

For compact bundle rollups, the workflow inspector also supports filesSummary:by=section, filesSummary:by=format, sort=-count, and top=<n>.

Boundary with DiffusionOPD

DiffusionOPD remains a diffusion-specific training path under gollek-train-diffusion-opd. Byte-latent language modeling should not be threaded through those packages just because both areas involve modern generative modeling.
